page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8y.xlarge is an ARM64-based compute-optimized instance powered by the custom Alibaba Yitian710 processor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core running at a clock speed of 2.75 GHz. The CPU is equipped with 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 64 MB L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the KVM hypervisor, includes no local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across several standard workloads. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yield scores of 1818.58 and 7235.59 respectively, placing them in the average tier. Memory bandwidth is measured at 408.75 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 74.83 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, cryptographic and extended instruction capabilities are limited, as evidenced by a weak PassMark CPU score of 3461.66 and a poor encryption test score of 651.04. Redis SET operations also show weak performance at 6.89 million operations per second.

The instance exhibits a clear tradeoff between raw compute efficiency and cryptographic processing. While static web serving throughput is stable at 6.85 GB/sec and small-model LLM text generation reaches an average of 128.91 tokens/sec, larger models like the 7B parameter LLM perform poorly at 4.69 tokens/sec. Given the lack of local storage and the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is suited for lightweight containerized microservices, static web serving, and basic multi-threaded data decompression tasks rather than memory-intensive databases or heavy cryptographic workloads.

It is configured with 8.0 GB of RAM, a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no local storage. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, the instance delivers average performance in multi-threaded decompression and static web serving, though it exhibits weak performance in cryptographic operations and database transactions.
